title: Connecting a new broker, step by step
text: From “Add channel” to a broker that is ready to go live, done live in the system.

title: Click “Add channel” to connect a new broker.
Type the broker’s name. To save time, copy the setup of a broker you already have.
text: Branches, booking rules, extras, terms and the rates are copied. Keys and contacts never are.

title: The channel code is the short name in the broker’s addresses, for example /ota/2024A/GCO/…
The new broker starts in Testing: its bookings are sandbox bookings and never hold a car.
text: Overview lists every setup step in order, with a link to the page where it is done.

title: Rates were copied as a draft. Check the prices for this broker, then publish them.
The publish window shows what changes. Publishing sends the prices to the broker as a new version.
Connection: new brokers use the “OpenTravel standard” layout, checked against the official OpenTravel rules.
text: Fill in the broker’s contacts and note the OpenTravel version they use.

title: Create the broker’s live key on the API keys page.
The key is shown only once, with a ready message for the broker. Send it securely, never in the same email as the documentation.
text: Only a fingerprint is stored: nobody can read the key back later.

title: Go-live: the certification test sends every broker message to the channel in the sandbox.
Each test shows its result. When the broker has tested too and the required items are done, “Approve go-live” switches the broker to real bookings.
